key_insight: GINNGER learns thermodynamic generators, not just constitutive operators, so the resulting rheology model is physically admissible by construction and generalizes across flow types.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-driven constitutive modeling of complex fluids that remains objective, interpretable, and consistent with the first and second laws of thermodynamics.
method: Embed the GENERIC framework into neural-network training to enforce thermodynamic structure.
Represent polymer conformation in its intrinsic spectral eigenspace to obtain a kinematics-independent state space.
Learn generators from microstructural flow data so shear, extensional, and mixed flows inform one shared model.
evidence_signal: Validated on high-fidelity simulations, the method reconstructs constitutive behavior and predicts complex flow fields in previously unseen geometries.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of training data, and the spectral state formulation may be sensitive to how conformation-tensor eigenstructures are computed near degeneracies.
paper_title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
